facts.heading: Anxiety worsens in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it gets worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Deputy head role
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school. She has taught at the school for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years and i love it.

facts.heading: Head asked Hannah to step up
facts.content: The head asked Hannah to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: the head asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking people picked the wrong person and she will be noticed as incompetent.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety manifests in evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxiety causes her chest to tighten and she rehearses meetings on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and i start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say regarding how others might perceive her.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what i would say and what they would think of me if i got it wrong

facts.heading: Imagined negative thoughts
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth or incapable.
facts.evidence: That i'm out of my depth, that they gave the job to a nice ear for a teacher who can't actually read

facts.heading: Rewriting email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of being perceived as stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves' treatment
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah. He told her he was delighted in September.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of pretense
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capability.
facts.evidence: I feel like i'm lying to him. About being capable, as if i'm pretending.

facts.heading: Identity comparison to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares her work to her mother's career. She thinks everything she does could have been done better by her mother.
facts.evidence: Everything i do, i think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's career influence
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years. A library is named after her.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years. She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says i've always worried too much and i should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hiding distress from mother
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad things are because she feels like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like i'm making a fuss, so i don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at 4 AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 every morning. She falls asleep fine.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine.

facts.heading: Waking through to-do list
facts.content: Hannah goes through a to-do list when awake at 4 AM. The list includes various items.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking since term started
facts.content: Hannah has been waking like this since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.heading: Drinks a lot of coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through the day. She knows this does not help.
facts.evidence: I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Five or six cups of coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee. This causes her difficulty sitting still in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: Five or six, then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

facts.heading: Heart races and hands shake
facts.content: Hannah's heart goes fast and her hands are shaky during the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water. She does not think anyone noticed.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted daily
facts.content: Hannah is exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Ben suggests Hannah should just enjoy her situation. Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when he says this.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it. Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's profession
facts.content: Ben is an engineer. He thinks if something is a problem, it can be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.

facts.heading: Difficulty with friends now
facts.content: Hannah is no longer able to talk to her friends at school.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Lost company with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with her promotion. She had not thought of it that way before.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Misses children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children most. She misses the daily experience of a child getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Wanted promotion but cried
facts.content: Hannah said yes to the promotion because she could not say no to the head. She went home and cried.
facts.evidence: I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her. Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Tears about not returning
facts.content: Hannah's tears were about a year and not getting to go back.
facts.evidence: A year I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays. They went walking in the lakes and she did not think about school for 10 days.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for 10 days.

facts.heading: Lack of expectation during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah. She was just talking and Ben carried the sandwiches.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just talking. Ben carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Wreck before term started
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down things that went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a chill laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks

facts.heading: Stopped writing due to feeling silly
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly about it.
facts.evidence: and then I stopped because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging. It just felt that way.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Wants to walk into meeting
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing at first.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first.

facts.heading: Wants to send one email
facts.content: Hannah wants to send an email only once.
facts.evidence: Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Wants to relax on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa on Sunday evenings without anxiety.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feels lighter after goals
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful when stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: Has not told anyone about 4am
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad the 4am experiences are.
facts.evidence: Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Scared to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben about the 4am experiences.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Might try telling Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben about the 4am this week.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Needs quiet moment to share
facts.content: Hannah needs a quiet moment to share information.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too wound up.

facts.heading: Suggests Saturday morning sharing
facts.content: Hannah suggests sharing on Saturday morning over breakfast.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood, Dan.

facts.heading: Wants to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah wants to try the evening notebook again for one week.
facts.evidence: Would you try the evening notebook again? just for a week. Even one line.
